reports.desc: A company by the name of billing services reached out with my full name (first and last) and attempted to collect $162.36 from me for various line items. I called the phone number that was provided and they requested the last four of my social as well as birth date and zip code. I said I was not comfortable giving that information over the phone and they said they couldn't tell me what company was billing me for these plans. The plans were made to sound like insurance premiums, one of which happened to sound halfway legit relative to my line of work. I feel convinced that this is a scam and wanted to report it.

I received a text message from 1-833-950-0621 from Illinoisfiling.com.  I pushed on the link and it wanted me to confirm all of my information.  Then it said pay $299.00 and I would never have to file again.  They sent it twice and asked for my banking information.  This is when I called the BBB to check to see if it was a scam.  It is a scam.

Since October 2025, I have received over 610 unsolicited prerecorded calls promoting supposed personal loans/debt relief. I have NEVER applied for a loan, answered these calls, returned a call, or consented to these solicitations. The callers continually rotate/spoof caller-ID numbers while directing recipients to recurring callback numbers using fictitious stories. Recent messages claim I have an existing “file,” that supervisors/underwriters have reviewed it, and, often lately, that numerous employees have repeatedly tried to reach me. This caller identified themself as "Frank" and offered an unsolicited $60,000 unsecured personal loan, saying i was one of a very few who had been approved. Other recordings use similar fictitious personal stories and loan approvals. I have preserved numerous voicemails, screenshots, dates, caller-ID numbers and callback numbers and have reported this to the FTC numerous times. This appears to be a large-scale, persistent robocall campaign, not isolated calls.

I received a rather threatening letter about losing the opportunity for my vehicle to have a warranty. There is little to no information about the sender of this letter other than the phone number. The letter claims they've been trying to contact me, though I have received no other emails, phone calls, or letters and if I don't call them by a date that's only a couple days away, I will be liable for any repairs to my car.
